messages:
maya: Heads up — p99 tail regression on H100 when seq_len > 512. Kernel dispatch is choosing CUTLASS for a bunch of workloads and p99 jumps ~30%. cc @raj @elena
perf-bot: Perf alert: job=seq-sweep/h100 run=2026-03-16 13:02 UTC | p50=22ms p95=78ms p99=128ms | baseline p99=98ms | profile: https://perf.redwood/internal/seq-sweep/h100/1972406789 :rotating_light:
raj: Do we have the selector config that switched cost model last night? I remember a change that biases toward throughput at batch>=8. Could be triggering CUTLASS picks even for mid seq lengths.
tony: Microbench results I ran locally: single-request seq=600, batch=8 => triton p99 ~96ms, cutlass p99 ~130ms. Throughput cost estimator is still favoring cutlass because it predicts better amortized tokens/s at that batch.
elena: Also seeing a lot of requests with large KV prefixes. Effective "execution" seq (KV+query) is higher than the client-reported seq. Selector uses estimated_effective_seq which might be inflated by KV cache logic.
maya: Snapshot of selector decision trace (short):
```
{selector_version: "v12.4", model: "rwkv-30b", hw: "h100", batch: 8, reported_seq: 600, kv_prefix: 320, effective_seq: 920, chosen_kernel: "cutlass", cost_est: 0.72, measured_latency_ms: 130}
```
raj: That effective_seq of 920 explains it. We should either cap the estimator or add hysteresis so transient KV spikes don't flip kernel. Current hysteresis window is 10s, maybe too small for bursty clients.
maya: Proposal: for H100 pools prefer Triton for effective_seq <= 1024 unless measured throughput delta > 20%. Add small dampening factor to kv contribution: effective_seq = reported_seq + 0.5 * kv_prefix.
tony: Quick patch I tested: change weight on kv_prefix from 1.0 -> 0.5, and add max cap: effective_seq = min(effective_seq, reported_seq + 512). On my bench p99 dropped from 128ms -> 104ms for same workload.
raj: We should also enable per-request telemetry: record chosen_kernel, estimated_cost, actual_latency to feed autotuner. Without that the selector can't learn the real tradeoffs.
elena: Agreed. Also watch batching heuristics: if aggregator averages seqs across batch we misestimate; set aggregator to use max(seq_i) not mean. That avoids "batch smearing" pushing kernel choice towards cutlass.
maya: I'll open a canary with the kv dampening + aggregator=max override + telemetry enabled. Canary will run on one h100 pool for 1h and collect autotune dump. If p99 improves or stays same we'll roll. If it gets worse >10% rollback.
infra-bot: Canary launched: h100-pool-12 | config: kv_weight=0.5, effective_seq_cap=512, aggregator=MAX | dashboard: https://canary.redwood/infer/h100/1972406789 | run_id=canary-1972406789
elena: Also add an autotune flag to persist decision traces for 1h: `--selector-log=decisions --flush-interval=10s` so we get enough samples.
maya: Nice. Can you add that to the canary run?
infra-bot: Updated canary run: selector logging enabled, traces streaming to /var/log/selector/canary-1972406789.log
tony: I'll tail the log and run the same synthetic load tonight to validate.
maya: Thanks team. Tag me if you see oscillation or p99 > baseline +10%.
raj: One more thing — add a short-term autotune experiment to try alternate cost-weight ratios (0.8, 1.0, 1.2) and compare real p99. We can automate ranking.
maya: Good idea. Adding a 3-arm micro-canary under same pool.
elena: ACK.
maya: :thumbsup:
